target_in_paper: Question 3.1(1) in §3.1 (Bounded cohomology of diffeomorphism groups): the Burago–Ivanov–Polterovich question asking whether Diff_0(S^3, vol) is uniformly perfect.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact target of the paper almost verbatim: it asks part (1) of Question 3.1, keeps the manifold S^3, uses the paper’s notation Diff_0(S^3, vol), and asks specifically about uniform perfectness rather than drifting to the neighboring quasimorphism question. In particular, retaining S^3 is correct: although the preceding contextual paragraph discusses Diff_0(S^2, vol), the official open question itself is stated for S^3.
missing_details: The notation Diff_0(S^3, vol) is not expanded; to make the question stand-alone, one should specify that after choosing a volume form ω on S^3, this denotes the identity component of the group of smooth ω-preserving diffeomorphisms of S^3.
The meaning of the subscript 0 should be stated explicitly: the connected component containing the identity map.
The shorthand 'vol' should be unpacked as preservation of the chosen volume form ω on S^3.
The phrase 'uniformly perfect' should be defined explicitly: there exists an integer N such that every element of the group can be written as a product of at most N commutators.
If full self-containment is desired, the regularity class should be made explicit: the paper is speaking about diffeomorphisms, i.e. smooth maps, not homeomorphisms.
refined_question: Let ω be a volume form on S^3, and let Diff_0(S^3, vol) denote the identity component of the group of smooth ω-preserving diffeomorphisms of S^3. Is Diff_0(S^3, vol) uniformly perfect, i.e. does there exist an integer N such that every element of Diff_0(S^3, vol) can be expressed as a product of at most N commutators?
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper. In §3.1, the paragraph immediately preceding Question 3.1 explains the intended notation by defining Diff_0(S^2, vol) as the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of S^2 in the identity component; Question 3.1 then asks the corresponding S^3 problem in two parts. So your draft is already paper-faithful in substance, and the only substantive upgrades needed are to spell out the notation and the meaning of uniform perfectness so the question stands on its own.
